content.title: "False Imprisonment" in Colorado - What are the penalties?
content.text: Top Denver criminal defense attorney discusses Colorado false imprisonment laws. Learn more about Colorado Legal Defense Group at https://www.shouselaw.com/co/defense or call (303) 222-0330 for a free consultation. FALSE IMPRISONMENT CRS 18-3-303 prohibits unlawfully detaining or confining a person without their consent. Examples of false imprisonment are locking people in a room or standing in a doorway in order to keep the people inside from getting out. Typical defenses to false imprisonment charges are that the victims consented or were free to leave. But it is not a defense if the victims managed to escape. What differentiates false imprisonment from the crime of kidnapping is that with false imprisonment, it is not necessary that the victim be moved. False imprisonment is typically a class 2 misdemeanor carrying up to 120 days in jail and/or a fine of up to $750. But false imprisonment becomes a class 5 felony in either of the following three circumstances: 1. The defendant used force – or threats of force – to confine or detain the victim. And the detention lasted for at least 12 hours. Or 2. The victim was under 18 and in a locked or barricaded room under circumstances that cause bodily injury or serious emotional distress. And the false imprisonment was part of a pattern of cruel punishment. Or 3. The victim was under 18 and confined by physical restraints under circumstances that cause bodily injury or serious emotional distress. Felony false imprisonment penalties include one to three years in prison and/or fines of $1,000 to $100,000.
